ruleSets.title: Bayesian differential database (pools, candidates, features, priors, likelihood ratios)
Bayesian differential engine parameters (pool routing, urgency boost, score boosts, confidence bands, feature DAG discounting)
Ask/order-next suggestions, clinical pipeline and algorithm prompts

History frames: chief complaint (+ system) -> symptom type -> the history questions asked (SOCRATES for pain only; cough, dyspnoea, lump, bleeding, bowel, dysphagia, jaundice and other frames), their chip options and the chip -> engine-feature mapping
Clinical scores and thresholds (101 score functions)
Automatic score inputs from the record (vitals, labs, history keywords)
Visit risk snapshot flags (NEWS2, anticoagulants, diabetes, BMI, pregnancy potential, timeline)
Wellness screening schedule (ScreeningEngine) and burns fluid data in PathwayData
iOS NICE NG12 suspected-cancer criteria and BSG 2021 IDA rule (Swift twin of cancer-screening 1.1.0) and the Diagnosis-tab prompt
Drug-interaction rules and drug classes (web and iOS, parity enforced)
Herbs, teas, bush remedies & supplements: catalogue, perioperative alerts and 'ask about' prompts (web and iOS, parity enforced)
Booking-email patient instructions, service pages, staff prep reference text and the dashboard's printed patient prep sheet / procedure leaflet
Public health-information library (patient-education articles on the website)
Web Bayesian differential (pane-engine): diseases, priors, feature likelihoods, prior modifiers, applicability, stopping rules; PANE feature mapper
Dashboard symptom-picker differential (adaptive Bayesian symptom inference)
Management protocols: investigations, phased management steps, medications with doses, red flags
Patient-specific plan filters: allergy cross-check, pregnancy, under-16 dosing, VTE, anticoagulation / antiplatelet / SGLT2 / steroid / anaesthetic / frailty lines
Decision support: score → guideline action, result → action, and treatment thresholds (Pauker–Kassirer observe / test / treat) personalised to the patient

What's missing — one ranked strip of the missing inputs the engines know about (safety basics, decision-layer inputs that flip a band, NG12 ferritin, best next discriminator, score completeness) and score auto-fill from the record
Sub-diagnosis variants and the management phases each may show
Triage rules: red-flag patterns, slot rules, exclusions, pathway definitions, reminder cascade, forbidden patterns
Staff adaptive triage: acuity scoring from symptoms, vitals and history
Recognise-and-redirect emergency layer: medical, obstetric, paediatric, neurological and surgical emergencies, safeguarding flags, risk modifiers
Cancer referral criteria (2-week-wait style) and internal-medicine referral detection
Preventive screening and surveillance (web port of the iOS ScreeningEngine, updated to USPSTF / ACG / US MSTF / ADA)

Lifestyle history (ritual fasting, complementary therapies, sleep / shift work): fasting and sleep safety prompts, evidence-graded non-drug plan suggestions, and the information-only questionnaire questions
Diagnosis radiation: suggested investigations, plan templates, billing codes, consent category, score criteria

iOS patient-specific plan filters (Swift twin of plan-safety-filters): allergy cross-check, pregnancy, under-16 doses and fluids, VTE, anticoagulation / antiplatelet / SGLT2 / steroid / anaesthetic / frailty lines
iOS triage level (max of CC keywords, vitals/NEWS2, BP, critical labs, ECG, text alarms, recognition rules, confirmed diagnosis), recognise-and-redirect alerts, pregnancy context
Perioperative surgical risk rules
Dashboard clinical scales and score calculators
Dashboard clinical decision support: score suggestions and clinical inference prompts
Diagnostic reasoning — zebra check (rare but real conditions for unusual combinations of findings)
Diagnostic reasoning — for/against thresholds, best-next-discriminator cost tiers, premature-closure guard, diagnostic time-out, longitudinal patterns

Diagnostic reasoning — web PANE adapter rules: working-diagnosis resolution, diagnosis families, two-conditions and already-named rules, web contradiction threshold, time-out coexisting states, can't-miss and coexisting lists
Practice laboratory reference ranges — built-in adult defaults (normal and critical limits) and the lookup every range / ULN / critical-limit consumer uses; iOS read-only twin, parity enforced
Laboratory feed — LOINC to catalogue analyte map, label fallback, exact MRN + date-of-birth matching, and 'flags never downgrade the laboratory'
Evidence-based examination signs: likelihood ratios (McGee / JAMA Rational Clinical Examination) feeding the web PANE and iOS Bayesian engines; Exam-step high-yield signs
Clinical decision rules as Bayesian evidence: band likelihood ratios (diagnostic) or risks (prognostic), the rule / component grouping policy, and the new rule calculators

items.group: I1. Patients may be told to stop herbal products 2 weeks before surgery — DECIDED 2026-09-25
items.title: Patients may be told to stop herbal products 2 weeks before surgery — DECIDED 2026-09-25
items.text:
- **Owner:** Dr Dawit Daniel Kabiye (practice owner), 2026-09-25, relayed with the herbs /
  supplements work (`docs/clinical-validation/changes/supplements-interactions.md`).
- **Decision:** patient-facing pre-op text MAY tell patients to stop herbal supplements 2 weeks
  before an operation or a procedure with sedation or an anaesthetic, and must give the reason and
  the circumstances. Prescribed medicines are unchanged: hazard H-10 still forbids take / hold /
  stop wording for them.
- **Approved text** (same words in `artifacts/front-desk/lib/instructions.ts` HERBAL_SUPPLEMENTS_STOP,
  `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/sms.ts` PREP_HERBAL, the dashboard's printed prep sheet and
  `supplement-catalogue.ts` / `SupplementCatalogue.swift`): "Herbal remedies, bush teas and
  supplements: please stop them 2 weeks before your operation or procedure. This includes garlic
  tablets, ginkgo, ginseng, ginger supplements, turmeric (curcumin), St John's wort, kava, echinacea,
  ashwagandha, ephedra (ma huang) and bush teas or herbal mixtures (tablets, capsules, extracts or
  strong teas — normal amounts in food are fine). Why: … When: … If your operation is less than 2
  weeks away, stop them now and tell the team what you take. If you take valerian every night, do
  not stop it suddenly — call the clinic. This does not apply to medicines prescribed by a doctor:
  do not stop any prescribed medicine unless the clinic tells you to. …"
- **Enforcement:** `lint:patient-instructions` and `outbound-safety.test.ts` allow stop wording only
  in the verbatim approved sentences, which name no prescribed medicine; tests confirm that stop
  wording with warfarin, aspirin, insulin, metformin, clopidogrel or "blood thinners" still fails.
- **Still open (not decided):** vitamin E and fish oil (not in the briefing); wording for emergency
  / urgent surgery; whether the pre-op assessment visit and minor procedures under local
  anaesthetic should carry the paragraph.

items.title: Treatment effects and harms
items.text:
**Treatment effects and harms** (B and H, as low / point / high). All are estimates:

| Decision | Option | B (low / point / high) | H (low / point / high) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Appendicitis | appendicectomy | .20 / .30 / .40 | .02 / .03 / .05 |
| Appendicitis | antibiotics-first | .14 / .22 / .30 | .01 / .015 / .03 |
| Cholecystitis | early LC | .20 / .30 / .40 | .04 / .07 / .10 |
| Cholecystitis | percutaneous cholecystostomy | .15 / .22 / .30 | .02 / .04 / .07 |
| Cholecystitis | antibiotics / supportive | .08 / .12 / .18 | .01 / .02 / .03 |
| Diverticulitis | antibiotics | −.01 / 0 / .02 | .01 / .02 / .03 |
| Diverticulitis | admission | −.01 / 0 / .02 | .01 / .02 / .04 |
| Upper GI bleed | admission and endoscopy within 24 h | .30 / .50 / .70 | .002 / .004 / .008 |
| Upper GI bleed | endoscopy within 12 h | 0 / 0 / .10 | .005 / .01 / .02 |
| Pulmonary embolism | anticoagulation | .10 / .20 / .30 | .008 / .015 / .025 |
| Pulmonary embolism | thrombolysis | −.07 / −.04 / −.01 | .05 / .07 / .10 |
| VTE prophylaxis | LMWH | .60 / .70 / .80 (relative reduction × risk) | .006 / .012 / .02 |
| VTE prophylaxis | mechanical | .30 / .50 / .60 | .001 / .002 / .005 |
| Sepsis | antibiotics within 1 h | .02 / .04 / .08 | .01 / .02 / .03 |
| Inguinal hernia | elective repair | .03 / .08 / .20 | .01 / .02 / .04 |
| Gallstone pancreatitis | same-admission cholecystectomy | .07 / .12 / .17 | .01 / .02 / .04 |
| Emergency laparotomy | emergency laparotomy | .30 / .50 / .70 | .04 / .08 / .12 |
| Peri-procedural bridging | LMWH bridging | .20 / .50 / .70 | .01 / .019 / .03 |

Several were tuned after sanity runs so the bands match the guideline answer: early LC, admission
for diverticulitis, hernia repair and LMWH. With them, a frail patient is steered to drainage,
Caprini 1 to mechanical prophylaxis, and a fit patient with uncomplicated diverticulitis to
observation. Please confirm that these are the answers you want.

items.title: The 28 global and 15 decision-specific modifiers
Risk bands
items.text:
**Risk bands.**
- GBS: 0–1 → 0.4%, 2–5 → 10%, 6–11 → 35%, ≥ 12 → 70% risk of needing an intervention.
- Caprini: 0 → 0.4%, 1–2 → 1.5%, 3–4 → 3%, ≥ 5 → 6% VTE risk.
- Wells PE: ≤ 4 → 12%, > 4 → 37%.
- Bridging:
  - baseline thromboembolic risk 0.4%;
  - mechanical valve **5% (an estimate, weighted for valve thrombosis)**;
  - VTE within 3 months 5%.

items.title: Engine rules
Net-benefit simplification
items.text:
**Net-benefit simplification:** extra harm from patient factors is taken off the benefit as
well, i.e. it is assumed to fall on patients with the disease too (`harmInDiseased` defaults to
true).

items.title: Default ULNs
items.text:
**Default ULNs** (lipase 60 U/L, amylase 100 U/L, hs-troponin T 14 ng/L) are placeholders. The
card tells the clinician to use the local laboratory's range. Please give the practice's
laboratory ranges.

items.title: Wording
items.text:
**Wording:** the qSOFA ≥ 2 and lactate ≥ 4 actions are written conditionally ("If suspected
infection, sepsis bundle now…"), so they do not assert sepsis in a patient who has, for example,
bleeding or ischaemia.

items.title: Recording scores for decision support
items.text:
**Recording scores for decision support:** "Use in decision support" writes the calculator
value to `clinical_scores.decisionScores` on the encounter. This is a new stored field in an
existing JSON column; no migration is needed.

items.title: "Add test"
items.text:
**"Add test"** adds to the orders on the web (the existing suggested-order path) and adds an
investigation with status "suggested" on iOS. Please confirm that this is acceptable, or
whether iOS should create an order instead.

items.title: For the differential owners (not changed here)
items.text:
**For the differential owners (not changed here):** the shift readout showed PANE moving
toward HHS on a raised glucose in a septic patient. That comes from the PANE weights, which this
change does not alter.

items.title: iOS runner
items.text:
**iOS runner:** `ClinValIOSRunner` reads `postOpDays` from the encounter to set "recent surgery
within 21 days". Please confirm that this matches how post-op day is recorded in the app.

items.title: Evidence thresholds
items.text:
**Evidence thresholds**: "for" LR ≥ 1.5, "against" LR ≤ 0.67, "favours" LR ≥ 2, "low evidence" =
no finding with LR ≥ 2; cardinal = P ≥ 0.6 and LR ≥ 2 (web) / stored logLR ≥ 8, LR ≈ 5 (iOS).

items.title: Premature-closure triggers
items.text:
**Premature-closure triggers**: a finding the working diagnosis models with LR ≤ 0.33 (present,
or a cardinal finding documented absent); "the record favours X" when X ≥ 50 %, ≥ 5 × the working
diagnosis and a named present finding has an LR ratio ≥ 10; NEWS2 rising by ≥ 2 to ≥ 5 (RCP
urgent-response threshold). Alert rate 77 / 397 vignettes with correct diagnoses — acceptable?

items.title: Coexisting states
items.text:
**Coexisting states** never offered as the alternative: sepsis, AKI, hyperkalaemia,
hypercalcaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoglycaemia (web ids; iOS by name).

items.title: Can't-miss list (web)
items.text:
**Can't-miss list (web)** that alone permits CT / MRI / endoscopy as the next discriminator (50
PANE diseases in `CANT_MISS_DISEASE_IDS`); iOS uses the database urgency ≥ 2.

items.title: Cost tiers and weights
items.text:
**Cost tiers and weights**: ask / bedside 1.0, lab 0.85, imaging 0.6, advanced 0.35; the term
lists that classify a test (e.g. ECG, urine dipstick, pregnancy test, capillary glucose and
ketones as bedside); minimum gain 0.01 nats.

items.title: iOS background rate
items.text:
**iOS background rate**: P(finding | diagnosis) = min(0.95, 0.05 × LR) for the information gain
and the post-test probabilities (the database stores LRs, not sensitivities); 5 % matches the
web's default background rate.

items.title: Time-out triggers
items.text:
**Time-out triggers**: ≥ 3 unexplained specific findings (web: symptoms, signs and results with a
background rate ≤ 5 %; iOS: non-history findings) or a repeat visit for the same complaint with no
diagnosis or changing diagnoses; the six checklist questions.

items.title: Zebra rule set
items.text:
**Zebra rule set** (16 rules): each rule's term groups, exclusions and citation — EoE; lead;
primary hyperparathyroidism (hypercalcaemia + 2 of stones / bones / groans / moans); Conn's
(hypertension + hypokalaemia, including on a diuretic); phaeochromocytoma (3 of headache, sweating,
palpitations, hypertension); hypertriglyceridaemia / autoimmune pancreatitis / IPMN (recurrent
pancreatitis with no affirmed gallstones or alcohol excess); aorto-enteric fistula; herb- or
supplement-induced liver injury; acute intermittent porphyria; Addison's; hereditary angioedema
(no urticaria); carcinoid; Zollinger-Ellison; Budd-Chiari.

items.title: Lab-derived terms
items.text:
**Lab-derived terms**: Hb < 11 g/dL (g/L above 25), adjusted calcium > 2.6 mmol/L (mg/dL above 5),
K < 3.5 / ≥ 6.0, Na < 130, eosinophils > 0.5 × 10⁹/L (cells/µL above 30), ALT/AST > 40 U/L,
bilirubin > 21 µmol/L (mg/dL below 5), triglycerides ≥ 11.3 mmol/L (mg/dL above 50).

items.title: Longitudinal thresholds
items.text:
**Longitudinal thresholds**: 3+ visits for a recurring presentation; creatinine rise ≥ 26.5 µmol/L
or ≥ 1.5 × the lowest earlier value (KDIGO 2012); Hb fall ≥ 20 g/L from the highest earlier value;
weight loss ≥ 5 % from the highest weight in the previous 183 days (NICE NG12 / MUST); an earlier
diagnosis is "revised" when a later one for the same problem shares no meaningful word.

items.title: "Add to differential" on iOS
items.text:
**"Add to differential" on iOS** appends "Differential (considered): X" to the assessment text
(iOS has no separate differential field); **"Add test to plan" on the web** appends a "Consider …"
line to the plan text rather than ordering.

items.title: PANE module sources
items.text:
**PANE module sources** shown as the evidence source for web LRs are the module-header guidelines
(`PANE_MODULE_SOURCES`); PANE has no per-feature citation.

items.title: Mapper clause rules
items.text:
**Mapper clause rules** (`record-text-match.ts`): per-item negation windows in "no A, B or C"
lists and "denies / never … and" lists; family-history markers; "not current" = a sentence
dated years back without an ongoing word, a repaired or awaiting / planned repair, a lay guess
— applied to PANE symptoms and signs and the injury mechanism.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Rule supersedes components
items.text: **Rule supersedes components**: while a decision rule is recorded, its component signs are neutral for its target diagnoses; a positive band adds only what the component findings have not already given (max rule); a band below 1 is applied in full.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: AIR supersedes Alvarado
items.text: **AIR supersedes Alvarado** when both are recorded.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: PERC is applied only when Wells PE is 4 or less
items.text: **PERC is applied only when Wells PE is 4 or less** (PERC is validated only in low pre-test probability).

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: LRINEC's low band is never applied
items.text: **LRINEC's low band is never applied** (LRINEC cannot rule out necrotising infection); its high band (6 or more) is applied with LR 4.5.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Prognostic rules are display only
items.text: **Prognostic rules are display only** (CURB-65, Glasgow-Blatchford, TG18 cholangitis severity, qSOFA, NEWS2, San Francisco syncope, Canadian syncope, Caprini, RCRI): they never change the differential.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Absence counts only when examined and meaningful
items.text: **Absence counts only when examined and meaningful**: an Absent chip updates the engine only for signs marked "absence used" below; unmarked signs are "not examined".

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Red-flag signs keep the engine's own weighting
items.text: **Red-flag signs keep the engine's own weighting** (twin mode: calf swelling, neck stiffness, focal deficit, papilloedema, mottling, new confusion, rigors, melaena on DRE, reduced anal tone): present sets the existing finding; the LR is shown but not applied; absence is never used.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Low-value signs are documentation only
items.text: **Low-value signs are documentation only** (Homans', Kernig's, Brudzinski's, obturator, pleural rub, adult capillary refill, Pemberton's, lower border of goitre, postural pulse, rectal tenderness).

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Only clinician-recorded rule results count
items.text: **Only clinician-recorded rule results count** ("Use in decision support" on web; the stored calculator result on iOS); values derived from vitals are not used.

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Secondary targets
items.text: **Secondary targets**: a sign's `alsoTargets` group gets sensitivity LR+ × (1 − specificity), capped at 0.95; rule-band base rate min(0.3, 0.9 / LR) and target probability min(0.99, LR × base rate) (web).

items.text: **New PANE node `cirrhosis`** "Cirrhosis / Chronic Liver Disease (Decompensated)", ICD-10 K74.60, prior tier uncommon, course chronic; P(finding | cirrhosis): known liver disease 0.80, alcohol 0.55, jaundice 0.45, ascites 0.50, abdominal distension 0.50, bilateral leg oedema 0.35, spider naevi 0.45, fatigue 0.55, anorexia 0.40, weight loss 0.25, confusion 0.15, thrombocytopenia 0.60, pruritus 0.20, dark urine 0.30, haematemesis 0.05, melaena 0.05, fever 0.10, progressive course 0.40 (Udell 2012; EASL 2018; Baveno VII).

items.title: New PANE node abdominal_wall_pain
items.text: **New PANE node `abdominal_wall_pain`** "Abdominal Wall Pain (e.g. Anterior Cutaneous Nerve Entrapment)", ICD-10 G58.8 (other specified mononeuropathy; please choose the code), prior tier uncommon, course chronic; localised pain 0.85, abdominal tenderness 0.95, RIF pain 0.30, RUQ 0.15, LIF 0.15, periumbilical 0.20, epigastric 0.10, worse on movement 0.50, episodic 0.40, previous surgery 0.30, nausea / vomiting 0.05, fever 0.02, raised WCC 0.02, anorexia 0.05 (Takada 2011; Scheltinga and Roumen 2018).

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: New iOS candidate "Abdominal Wall Pain (Anterior Cutaneous Nerve Entrapment)"
items.text: **New iOS candidate "Abdominal Wall Pain (Anterior Cutaneous Nerve Entrapment)"** (G58.8), logPrior −5 (uncommon), urgency 0, in `coreConditions` and the abdominal-pain presentation; features: abdominal complaint logLR +1 (LR 1.3, expert estimate), pain at one fingertip-sized spot +5 (LR 3), fever −6 (LR 0.3) (no duration feature: the history step's duration chips are record-only on iOS).

items.group: Policy and new content
items.title: Target groups
items.text: **Target groups** (which diagnoses a sign's LR applies to, web PANE ids and iOS name fragments) as listed in `clinical-content/rules/exam-signs.json` `targetGroups` — e.g. peritonism → appendicitis, perforated ulcer, diverticulitis, anastomotic leak, post-operative collection, toxic megacolon, abdominal trauma; nodal malignancy → gastric, oesophageal, pancreatic, thyroid, breast, melanoma, anal and skin SCC (and lymphoma on iOS).

items.title: History frame → examination
items.text: **History frame → examination** (`exam-signs.json` `frames`): for each of the 41 history frames, the iOS examination region and its chips (`ExamRegion.swift`), the web systems shown and the presentation tags offered (e.g. cough → chest / respiratory, CURB-65 and the pneumonia signs; groin lump → groin / hernia signs; lump elsewhere → local lump chips and lymph nodes; unrecognised complaint → general examination).

Policy: display only; iOS calculator
Source, quality: Lim WS et al. Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital, Thorax 2003;58:377-82; NICE NG138 / BTS 2009; single study.

items.title: Centor / McIsaac score (diagnostic)
items.text:
Decision rule (kind): Centor / McIsaac score (diagnostic)
Target finding: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis

Absence / low band used: yes
Policy: iOS calculator
Source, quality: McIsaac WJ et al. CMAJ 1998; Aalbers J et al. Predicting streptococcal pharyngitis in adults in primary care: a systematic review, BMC Med 2011; NICE NG84 (FeverPAIN / Centor); pooled meta-analysis.

items.text:
Decision rule (kind): STONE score (ureteric stone) (diagnostic)
Target finding: Uncomplicated ureteric stone
Bands (score range: LR or risk): 0-5: low probability (about 10 %) (0–5): LR 0.10 (0.06–0.16); 6-9: moderate probability (about 51 %) (6–9): LR 1.0 (0.80–1.2); 10-13: high probability (about 89 %) (10–13): LR 7.8 (5.0–12)
Absence / low band used: yes

Target finding: Need for transfusion, endoscopic therapy or surgery (upper GI bleed)
Bands (score range: LR or risk): 0-1: very low risk (0–1): risk Intervention or death under 1 % (outpatient management may be considered); 2-7 (2–7): risk Intermediate risk: inpatient endoscopy; 8 or more (≥ 8): risk High risk: early endoscopy

items.text:
Decision rule (kind): qSOFA (prognostic)
Target finding: In-hospital death or prolonged ICU stay in suspected infection
Bands (score range: LR or risk): 0-1 (0–1): risk Lower risk; qSOFA is insensitive, so keep screening with NEWS2; 2-3 (2–3): risk In-hospital mortality roughly 3 to 14 times higher: assess for organ dysfunction

items.title: Turning the database on at all
items.text:
**Turning the database on at all.** 2.0.0 decodes, so the iOS differential switches from the
built-in lists to this content on the next app build. The CLAUDE.md gotcha says this needs the
surgeon's sign-off and the vignette suite. Conservative alternative: ship the engine fixes with
the database file held back (the fallback lists stay in use).

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Prior tiers
items.text:
**Prior tiers** (common / uncommon / rare = 0 / −5 / −10) for all 121 curated candidates (table)
and the rank-derived tiers of the 1.0.0 pools. They are condition-neutral population estimates,
not per-complaint probabilities.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Caps on the 1.0.0 content
items.text:
**Caps on the 1.0.0 content** (±8 / ±12 / ±5 / +5 / +3). The alternative is to review the 1,232
legacy candidates one by one; until then they are unreviewed.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Urgency boost removed; two "do not miss" places
items.text:
**Urgency boost removed; two "do not miss" places** (ranks 4–5 for urgency ≥ 2). Conservative
alternative: three places (ranks 3–5), which shows more dangerous diagnoses and fewer probable
ones.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Complaint-weight features
items.text:
**Complaint-weight features** (key `complaint`, 130 features cited "expert estimate pending the
surgeon's review"): LR 1.2–4 for the presenting complaint matching a candidate. No published LR
exists for these.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: notFinding likelihood ratios
items.text:
**`notFinding` likelihood ratios** (49 candidates, LR 0.1–0.4): e.g. no chest, arm, jaw,
epigastric or breathing symptom for ACS (LR 0.3, Canto JAMA 2000 — atypical ACS is real);
no operation with an anastomosis for anastomotic leak (0.1); no alcohol history for alcoholic
hepatitis (0.1).

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Applicability and pregnancy
items.text:
**Applicability and pregnancy.** Pregnancy is read from free text (no Patient field): a pregnant
patient whose notes never say so will not see pregnancy-only diagnoses (pre-eclampsia / HELLP,
abruption, hyperemesis). Ectopic pregnancy is "possible" in females 10–55 unless pregnancy is
recorded as excluded. Needs obstetric sign-off.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Children's vital-sign limits
items.text:
**Children's vital-sign limits** (APLS 7th edition bands; age 0 = infant band, so an adult without
a date of birth gets fewer tachycardia / tachypnoea chips, never more). Needs paediatric sign-off.

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Numeric laboratory thresholds
items.text:
**Numeric laboratory thresholds** (engine change 7), including the unit-guessing rule (calcium
≥ 5 read as mg/dL, glucose ≥ 100 as mg/dL, haemoglobin ≥ 25 as g/L).

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Content decisions listed above
items.text:
**Content decisions listed above** (cholecystitis, acalculous, alcoholic and viral hepatitis,
TSS, ischaemic colitis, achalasia, oesophageal cancer, anaplastic thyroid, hernia, CAP, leak).

items.group: Surgeon (and, where marked, physician / obstetric / paediatric colleagues) before release
items.title: Medical, obstetric and paediatric candidates
items.text:
**Medical, obstetric and paediatric candidates** (ACS, PE, AF, HF, anaphylaxis, DKA / HHS,
hypoglycaemia, stroke, SAH, meningitis, sepsis, pre-eclampsia / HELLP, ectopic, intussusception,
pyloric stenosis, malrotation and the rest of the table): content outside general surgery that
a physician, obstetrician or paediatrician should check.

items.title: Matrix skipped when a presentation matches
items.text:
**Matrix skipped when a presentation matches** (its system-wide extras were unreviewed noise);
complaints matching no presentation still use it.

items.title: HPI now read by the differential
items.text:
**HPI now read by the differential.** Findings written only in the HPI now count; a negation the
matcher misses ("not able to pass urine" is read as affirmed "pass urine") can now affect the
list.

items.title: Citations
items.text:
**Citations.** Every citation was written from the literature without a check against the
source; each must be verified before the registry's `lastReviewed` is set.

items.text:

items.text: ABCD2: note only (calculator kept) vs removal.

items.title: Every likelihood and sensitivity
items.text: **Every likelihood and sensitivity** in `vademecum/specialties/*.ts`. These are approximations of published ranges and have not been checked against the sources.

items.title: Prior tiers
items.text: **Prior tiers** (0.03 / 0.015 / 0.007 / 0.003 / 0.001) and the tier given to each disease (table above).

items.title: Background rates
items.text: **Background rates.** The default is 0.05 for an unmodelled finding, plus the per-feature `baseRate` values and the derived/correlated defaults in `engine/likelihood.ts`.

items.title: PREGNANCY_POSSIBLE_MULTIPLIER = 5
items.text: **`PREGNANCY_POSSIBLE_MULTIPLIER = 5`** for pregnancy-only nodes when "pregnancy possible" is ticked. Pregnancy-only nodes are excluded for male patients and outside ages 10–55.

items.title: Gate inference
items.text: **Gate inference.** A full record with no mention of trauma, an operation in the last 30 days, an aortic graft or a stoma is read as their *absence*. This is the only absence inference in the mapper.

items.title: Lab thresholds
items.text: **Lab thresholds** in the mapper (list above), and the **paediatric vital thresholds** (APLS).

items.title: Adult-predominant ×0.05 under 16
items.text: **Adult-predominant ×0.05 under 16** (PANE) and **childhood entries ×0.05 / ×0.3 from 16** (symptom inference).

items.title: Caribbean diabetes tier adjustment
items.text: **Caribbean diabetes tier adjustment** (IDF Atlas 2021).

items.title: Sex likelihood ratios
items.text: **Sex likelihood ratios**, e.g. inguinal hernia M:F 9 → ×1.8 men / ×0.2 women, down from ×5 / ×0.3. There is no longer any boost for women on gynaecological or breast nodes.

items.title: thermal_burn_major ICD-10 T31.30 → T31.20
items.text: **`thermal_burn_major` ICD-10 T31.30 → T31.20.** This is the TBSA 20–29 % band, the typical case in the vignettes. A burn of 30 % or more should code as T31.3x. The surgeon may prefer an unspecified TBSA code.

items.title: Colorectal cancer
items.text: **Colorectal cancer** in anticoagulated diverticular LGIB is now rank 4, below lower GI haemorrhage, upper GI haemorrhage and mesenteric ischaemia (`lgib-diverticular-apixaban/mnm-crc`). Should CRC be forced into the top 3 for LGIB at 60+? The conservative choice was not to add a boost that is not in a guideline.

items.title: SGLT2 inhibitors before a procedure
items.text:
**SGLT2 inhibitors before a procedure**: CPOC 2021 "day before and day of" is used; FDA labelling
says 3 days (4 for ertugliflozin). The line names both — the surgeon chooses.

items.title: P2Y12 before high-risk endoscopy
items.text:
**P2Y12 before high-risk endoscopy**: 7 days (BSG/ESGE 2021) and before surgery clopidogrel 5 /
ticagrelor 3–5 / prasugrel 7 days (ESC/ESAIC 2022).

items.title: Stent windows
items.text:
**Stent windows**: 6 months after elective PCI, 12 months after ACS — defer unless cardiology
agrees (ESC/ESAIC 2022).

items.title: Burns fluids (D1/D2)
E1
items.text:
**E1**: "strangulation not excluded" keeps the strangulated (emergency) variant — the conservative
choice; the vignette expects the incarcerated variant (quality, still flagged).

items.title: E5
items.text: **E5**: no parathyroid variant group; confirm whether one is wanted.

items.title: resolveProtocol rule
items.text:
**resolveProtocol rule**: a more specific recorded ICD code overrides the working diagnosis's
protocol (e.g. IDC + N63 → breast-lump triple assessment; thyroid carcinoma + D44.0 → nodule
protocol by Bethesda). Confirm this is the behaviour wanted.

items.title: Guideline sources to confirm
items.text:
**Guideline sources to confirm**: intussusception reduction technique (APLS + local practice);
amoebic abscess (BNF only); pharyngeal pouch (NICE IPG22, 2003); adult intussusception branch (no
single guideline); post-operative pyrexia (clinical practice); pyloric stenosis and malrotation
(APLS + BAPS practice).

items.title: Frailty/delirium trigger
items.text:
**Frailty/delirium trigger**: age ≥ 65 with frailty, CFS ≥ 5, dementia, cognitive impairment or
previous delirium, or age ≥ 80, when a procedure or acute illness is planned.

items.title: Emergency-surgery anticoagulant line
items.text:
**Emergency-surgery anticoagulant line**: PCC discussion for factor Xa inhibitors before surgery
(andexanet is licensed for life-threatening bleeding, not surgery) — ESC/ESAIC 2022; confirm with
local haematology.

items.title: NSAIDs before 20 weeks
items.text: **NSAIDs before 20 weeks**: annotated ("only if the benefit outweighs the risk"), not withheld.

items.title: Phaeochromocytoma, femoral artery aneurysm, post-operative collection, toxic megacolon
items.text:
**Phaeochromocytoma, femoral artery aneurysm, post-operative collection, toxic megacolon** use
the closest existing protocol (adrenal incidentaloma, aortic aneurysm, SSI organ/space, UC) via
aliases; dedicated protocols may be preferred.

items.title: Fasting
items.text:
**Fasting** in the Plan-tab nursing orders now follows AAGBI 2010 / ESA 2011 (6 h food, 2 h
clear fluids) instead of "NPO from midnight" (clinician-facing only; the patient-facing prep
texts are unchanged).

items.title: Cellulitis Eron classes
items.text:
**Cellulitis Eron classes**: the plan still lists the oral Eron I option next to the IV options
for a septic patient (`cellulitis-sepsis-elderly-diabetic/mgmt-no-oral-only`, quality, fails on
both the base and this branch); a severity branch needs a decision (NICE NG141 first line is
flucloxacillin; the protocol uses phenoxymethylpenicillin).

items.title: Rule set
items.text:
**Rule set**: USPSTF as the primary screening source for this practice, ACG/US MSTF for
colonoscopy and polyp surveillance, NCCN/ACR for high-risk breast, ADA 2024 for diabetes, NICE
NG136 for BP confirmation (G2.19 answered "USPSTF").

items.title: Rectal bleeding ≥ 50
items.text:
**Rectal bleeding ≥ 50**: direct 2-week-wait referral (NG12 2015). NG12's 2023 update puts FIT
first for this group; direct referral was kept as the more conservative option.

items.title: IDA
items.text: **IDA**: ferritin cut-off 45 µg/L (BSG 2021) and age ≥ 50 as a stand-in for post-menopausal status.

items.title: PSA
items.text:
**PSA**: discussion from 45 with a family history of prostate cancer or BRCA (ACS 2023); whether
African-Caribbean ancestry alone should also start at 45 (iOS does; web has no ancestry input).

items.title: Hepatitis B
items.text:
**Hepatitis B**: universal once-in-adulthood screening (CDC 2023) rather than USPSTF 2020
risk-based screening.

items.title: Diabetes
items.text: **Diabetes**: screening every adult from 35 (ADA 2024; USPSTF 2021 limits to overweight 35–70).

items.title: Lynch aspirin
items.text:
**Lynch aspirin**: discussion only; the dose is the clinician's (NICE NG151 does not fix it in
this item).

items.title: Oral iron wording
items.text:
**Oral iron wording**: "one tablet daily or on alternate days" (BSG 2021) with the preparation left
to the prescriber.

items.title: Consultation suspected-cancer prompt scope
items.text:
**Consultation suspected-cancer prompt scope**: shows the 1.1.0 criteria only; the older chip rules
(dysphagia, jaundice ≥ 40, breast lump ≥ 30) stay triage-banner only.

items.title: Removal of the osteoporosis vitamin D / calcium dose line
items.text: Removal of the osteoporosis vitamin D / calcium dose line.

items.title: Local safeguarding contacts
items.text:
**Local safeguarding contacts**: the practice must supply its local safeguarding and
domestic-abuse contacts. The flags say only "follow the practice's safeguarding procedure".

items.title: Dilated CBD threshold
items.text:
**Dilated CBD threshold**: > 6 mm, or > 8 mm after cholecystectomy, with no age adjustment. Some
sources allow roughly 1 mm per decade over 60.

items.title: NEWS2 mapping
items.text: **NEWS2 mapping**: a single red score (low-medium band) → urgent (same-day call), not priority.

items.title: Troponin rule-in 52 ng/L
items.text:
**Troponin rule-in 52 ng/L**: ESC 2023 value for hs-cTnT. It depends on the assay; the practice
laboratory's assay and cut-off need confirming.

items.title: Postpartum timing
items.text:
**Postpartum timing**: when the text says "postpartum" without a number of weeks, ≤ 6 weeks is
assumed. This affects pre-eclampsia, VTE and β-HCG prompts.

items.title: Scrotal pain
items.text:
**Scrotal pain**: acute scrotal pain is always an emergency (torsion until proven otherwise). This
over-triages epididymo-orchitis.

items.title: Acute pelvic pain
items.text:
**Acute pelvic pain** in a woman of reproductive age with a positive or unknown pregnancy test →
emergency (ectopic).

items.title: Adrenaline stock (G1.2)
items.text:
**Adrenaline stock (G1.2)**: the anaphylaxis prompt assumes IM adrenaline 1 mg/mL is available in
clinic.

items.title: Aspirin in suspected ACS
items.text:
**Aspirin in suspected ACS**: 150–300 mg suggested (ESC 2023), unless allergic or bleeding. It is
never auto-applied.

items.title: Sepsis
items.text: **Sepsis**: moderate-risk criteria → urgent (same-day call); high-risk → emergency.

items.title: Hyperkalaemia 6.0–6.4 mmol/L
items.text: **Hyperkalaemia 6.0–6.4 mmol/L** without ECG changes → urgent, not emergency.

items.title: Calcium thresholds
Paediatric vital bands
items.text:
**Paediatric vital bands**: HR / RR from NICE NG51 / NG143; SBP from PALS (70 + 2 × age). The bands
are a combination of sources, not one table.

items.title: P2Y12 stopping times

items.title: Classifier precedence
items.text:
**Classifier precedence**: lump / breast before symptoms before administrative words; then the
earliest keyword. E.g. "painful lump" → lump history, "cough and chest pain" → cough history with
chest pain as a secondary symptom, "Reflux / Heartburn" → chest pain SOCRATES, "Rectal prolapse" →
bowel habit history, "Leg swelling" → limb swelling history.

joint, Cardiovascular / Respiratory → chest, Neurology → head, Dermatology → limb, otherwise
abdomen).

items.text:

evidence (DKA in a diabetic, AAA in an older man, incarcerated hernia) take "do not miss" places

items.title: Report evidence
items.text:
**Report evidence** (engine 3): a curated diagnosis with a feature of LR ≥ 10 in a resulted report
or laboratory chip is added whatever the complaint. Threshold (logLR 12) and the rule that the
history never adds one.

items.title: Post-operative day from the text
items.text:
**Post-operative day from the text** (engine 2): the patterns, the "earlier episode" exclusions and
"smallest day wins". Neck haematoma day 0–1 LR 3 and day ≥ 7 LR 0.2 (Iliff 2022); anastomotic leak
day 3–30 LR 2 (Hyman 2007; replaces "day 3" … "day 9", same LR).

items.title: Masking contexts
items.text:
**Masking contexts** (engine 2): definitions (elderly ≥ 65; the immunosuppression and diabetes word
lists; female) and the two uses — perforated ulcer "no guarding / rigidity / peritonism" LR 0.4
masked in the elderly and immunosuppressed; ACS "chest pain documented absent" LR 0.5 masked in
women, older people and diabetes (physician).

items.text:

from the time of the symptoms); LRINEC ≥ 6 from the results on file, LR 4.5 (Fernando 2019), missing
items scored 0. Note for review: the app's LRINEC calculator scores creatinine > 177 µmol/L as +4
(Wong 2004 has a single > 141 µmol/L band of +2); not changed here.

items.title: PE
ACS atypical presentation
items.text:
**ACS atypical presentation**: epigastric pain or "indigestion" with sweating LR 2 (expert; Canto
2000, NICE CG95); jaw / arm ache and exertional-symptom wording widened (Swap & Nagurney LRs
unchanged); "heavy" added to pressure-type pain (physician).

items.title: Boerhaave

items.title: Aorto-enteric fistula
items.text:

LR 0.2 (expert); herald-bleed wording.

items.title: NSTI
Cellulitis
items.text:
**Cellulitis**: erythema with warmth and tenderness LR 3, raised WBC or CRP LR 2, red swollen /
hot limb complaint LR 1.5 (all expert, IDSA 2014). These are what put cellulitis in the top 3 of
`cellulitis-sepsis-elderly-diabetic` (margin 3).

items.title: Cholecystitis in fever
PID
items.text:
**PID**: tubo-ovarian abscess / pyosalpinx on imaging LR 10 (expert; Lareau 2008); "tender adnexal"
wording.

items.title: Mesenteric ischaemia
items.text:
**Mesenteric ischaemia**: age ≥ 75 LR 2 (Kärkkäinen 2015) on top of age ≥ 60 LR 2; supersedes
legacy NOMI. Not modelled on purpose: anticoagulation lowering the risk (the vignette asks for AMI
to stay listed in an anticoagulated 78-year-old with AF).

items.title: New negatives
items.text:
**New negatives**: C. difficile no diarrhoea LR 0.2 (IDSA/SHEA 2017); anaphylaxis no skin, mucosal
or airway feature LR 0.2 (Campbell 2012; WAO 2020) (physician); incarcerated hernia no hernia /
groin / abdominal-wall sign LR 0.2 (expert, HerniaSurge 2018); ischaemic colitis no bleeding or
diarrhoea LR 0.3 (ACG 2015); DKA acidosis without ketones LR 2 (was part of the LR-10 ketone
feature) and the DKA "no feature" negative now needs a raised glucose, diabetes, ketones, acidosis
or an SGLT2 inhibitor (a normal glucose result no longer cancels it) (physician); hypercalcaemia
cause wording ("PTH").

items.title: Tightened LR ≥ 10 features
items.text:
**Tightened LR ≥ 10 features** (report evidence exposed them): oesophago-gastric carcinoma (now
needs the oesophagus / stomach), DVT (a deep vein), DKA (ketones), anastomotic leak (the
anastomosis; free fluid / gas / collection alone LR 3), liver abscess (the liver), stroke (brain
imaging wording), obturator hernia ("knee pain" alone no longer the Howship-Romberg sign), Charcot
foot, pericardial rub, acute cholecystitis (the gallbladder). Check that no true presentation is
now missed.

items.title: Citations
items.text:
**Citations**: written from the literature without a check against the source; each must be
verified before `lastReviewed` is set.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: NSAID exclusions on every plan line
items.text:
**NSAID exclusions on every plan line.** The web applies them to its operative-template analgesia
line; iOS withholds any line proposing an NSAID (card, SOAP, pipeline) for renal impairment (CKD,
dialysis, eGFR < 60), age ≥ 75, heart failure, ulcer / GI bleed history or an anticoagulant —
prophylactic enoxaparin counts, as on the web. Lines that stop / avoid an NSAID are kept.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Pregnancy added to the NSAID reasons
items.text:
**Pregnancy added to the NSAID reasons** of the operative analgesia line (the web line offers
ibuprofen "if renal function is normal" in pregnancy; its pregnancy prompt forbids NSAIDs from 20
weeks).

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Stable GI bleeding needs a recorded SBP or heart rate
items.text:
**Stable GI bleeding needs a recorded SBP or heart rate** on iOS (the web treats missing vital signs
as stable). A stable upper GI bleed keeps a restrictive-transfusion line (Hb 70 / 80 g/L) the web
stable line leaves out, because two high-Blatchford vignettes expect it.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: UKKA bands apply only with a recorded potassium and no ECG change written
items.text:
**UKKA bands apply only with a recorded potassium and no ECG change written** (hyperkalaemic ECG
changes keep the full card). K⁺ below 5.5 also withholds shift therapy.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Colonic stent rule
items.text:
**Colonic stent rule** (web sign-off item 2): the same contraindications and right-sided sites; on
iOS it also rewrites stent lines from the SOAP vademecum and the pipeline.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: D-dimer withheld in pregnancy
items.text:
**D-dimer withheld in pregnancy** on every line (RCOG GTG 37a/b); the web only states it is
unhelpful. After recent surgery iOS only states it (PE card), as the web does.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Occult-malignancy CT withheld in pregnancy
items.text:
**Occult-malignancy CT withheld in pregnancy** on every line; CT abdomen / pelvis in a child or in
pregnancy is annotated (not removed).

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Injury on an anticoagulant
items.text:
**Injury on an anticoagulant**: injury words are read from the CC, HPI, diagnosis and assessment
("fell", "fall at home / down / from / onto / on", head injury, trauma, collision, assault,
fracture); a head injury without a documented bleed no longer triggers the bleeding note. Vitamin K
antagonists and DOACs only (heparins not included).

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Clotting screen
items.text:
**Clotting screen** (web sign-off item 11): added as a patient-specific investigation before
surgery; "emergency" is read from the assessment text.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Operative-template lines on cards
items.text:
**Operative-template lines on cards**: added to cholecystectomy, appendicectomy and hernia cards
for adults only (not under 16, not on recognise-and-redirect cards); SIGN 104 high-risk list and
HerniaSurge wording as web sign-off items 5 and 6.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Operative-plan default
items.text:
**Operative-plan default**: "single dose at induction only if indicated (SIGN 104 / local policy)"
replaces "Co-amoxiclav 1.2 g IV at induction" for new plans.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Relatives' history entries
items.text:
**Relatives' history entries**: a clause naming a relative (mother, father, sister, brother,
parents, aunt, uncle, grandparent, cousin, relative, family history) is dropped from the pipeline
PMH flags and the new rules — a single clause such as "Type 2 diabetes — father also diabetic"
would be dropped too.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: TG18 age ≥ 75
items.text:
**TG18 age ≥ 75** (web sign-off item 1): iOS used > 75; now ≥ 75 in the auto-fill and the item
label. Metaraminol and vasopressin count as vasopressors.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Diabetic foot (NICE NG19)
items.text:
**Diabetic foot (NICE NG19)**: "infected diabetic foot" / "exposed bone" urgent, "diabetic foot" /
"foot wound" priority. **Gangrene stays an emergency term on iOS** (web: urgent red flag) because the
same term covers gangrenous bowel, gallbladder and Fournier's gangrene.

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Wells PE calculator
items.text:
**Wells PE calculator**: the low / moderate display bands are kept; both now recommend D-dimer first
(two-level Wells).

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Penicillin
items.text:
**Penicillin**: iOS keeps withholding a penicillin line even when it also names the allergy
alternative (the web leaves such a line as written); immediate reactions still withhold
cephalosporins and carbapenems (ios-plan-safety sign-off item 1).

items.group: Deliberate iOS differences and new iOS choices
items.title: Pre-operative potassium alert
items.text: **Pre-operative potassium alert**: calcium gluconate "if ECG changes" and salbutamol only ≥ 6.5.

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Beta-lactams after an immediate penicillin reaction
items.text: **Beta-lactams after an immediate penicillin reaction.** After an immediate or severe penicillin reaction (anaphylaxis, angio-oedema, urticaria, bronchospasm, "severe"), iOS **withholds** cephalosporins and carbapenems. The web only cautions (BNF allows some with specialist advice).

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Thrombolysis on an oral anticoagulant
items.text: **Thrombolysis on an oral anticoagulant.** Thrombolysis (alteplase, tenecteplase) is withheld on any oral anticoagulant, with thrombectomy discussion (NICE NG128; ESO 2021; ESC 2019). This covers plan lines and now referral reasons, e.g. "thrombolysis window 4.5 h". Web has no such rule.

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: VTE line on request
items.text: **VTE line on request.** The NICE NG89 line is added whenever the assessment mentions VTE prophylaxis, thromboprophylaxis, VTE risk or Caprini, even with no operation.

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Inferred "not pregnant"
items.text: **Inferred "not pregnant".** Not-pregnant is inferred from "post-menopausal", "total hysterectomy", "not pregnant" or a negative test in the text. A male patient is never flagged for β-hCG.

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: "NSAID contraindicated" counts as not given
items.text: **"NSAID contraindicated" counts as not given.** Wording such as "NSAID contraindicated" or "not tolerated" after a drug name is treated as not given.

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Peri-procedural wording
items.text: **Peri-procedural wording.** The DOAC before high-risk endoscopy line reads "stop … 3 days before the procedure". The mechanical-valve line reads "bridging … is indicated for a mechanical valve".

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Past laparotomy
items.text: **Past laparotomy.** The NELA line ignores a past laparotomy ("day 3 after laparotomy").

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: DOAC renal function
items.text: **DOAC renal function.** The CrCl investigation is added even when the card lists "U&E".

items.group: Deliberate differences from the web filter
items.title: Filter scope
items.text: **Filter scope.** Referral reasons and notes go through the line filter too.

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Thyroid card
items.text: **Thyroid card.** A single card graded by Bethesda I–VI. Hot nodule: no FNA, then radioiodine or hemithyroidectomy. Bethesda III–IV: diagnostic lobectomy. Bethesda V–VI: MDT, lobectomy or total thyroidectomy. N1b: lateral neck dissection.

items.title: Pre-operative card

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Local UTI treatment days
items.text: **Local UTI treatment days.** The nitrofurantoin duration was kept at 5 days (St Lucia local choice), now "lower UTI / cystitis only".

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Hypertensive emergency card
items.text: **Hypertensive emergency card.** It is a recognise-and-redirect card (outpatient clinic). IV labetalol, nicardipine or GTN are named as first actions in a monitored setting.

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Febrile infant card
items.text: **Febrile infant card.** It is a recognise-and-redirect card (NICE NG143).

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Hernia decision
items.text: **Hernia decision.** The emergency hernia decision is renamed to "surgical review", and repair is only "if strangulation is confirmed".

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Lactate ≥ 4 line
items.text: **Lactate ≥ 4 line.** The line is "goal-directed resuscitation (fluid volume by cause of shock)", with no fixed 30 mL/kg.

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Alarm terms
items.text: **Alarm terms.** "Perforated viscus" and "free intraperitoneal / extraluminal gas" raise the perforation alarm.

items.group: Content choices
items.title: "Charcot" alias
items.text: **"Charcot" alias.** The vademecum alias "Charcot" was narrowed to "Charcot's triad" (it had matched Charcot foot).

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Gangrenous sigmoid volvulus
items.text: **Gangrenous sigmoid volvulus.** The line reads "sigmoid resection and end colostomy", no longer "Hartmann's procedure".

items.group: Content choices
items.title: Line removal
items.text: **Line removal.** Pregnancy and renal line replacements remove a whole pipeline action ("⚠ … withheld (contains …)"), including other content on that line. This is the same as the web.

items.title: Screening rule set on iOS
items.text:
**Screening rule set on iOS**: the same USPSTF / ACG / US MSTF / NCCN / ACR / ADA / NICE NG136
choices as the web (fix-web-screening.md sign-off items 1, 5, 6, 7 apply to iOS too).

items.title: PSA from 45 for African-Caribbean ancestry alone
items.text:
**PSA from 45 for African-Caribbean ancestry alone** (iOS keeps it; the web has no ancestry
input and starts at 45 only with a family history or BRCA). Choose one rule for both.

items.title: No PSA investigation offered
items.text:
**No PSA investigation offered** from the screening list (web parity): the PSA is ordered only
after the shared decision.

items.title: BRCA carrier item from 18
items.text:
**BRCA carrier item from 18** (MRI offered from 25), and the breast family-history item from 25
(was 30 on iOS).

items.title: Colorectal family history under 40
items.text:
**Colorectal family history under 40**: a "due from 40" item without a test; the clinician must
check the youngest relative's age (iOS has no field for it). Add the field?

items.title: Lynch-family genetics item shown alongside polyp surveillance
items.text:
**Lynch-family genetics item shown alongside polyp surveillance** on iOS (the web hides it when
polyps are recorded) — which behaviour should both platforms have?

items.title: Lipids from 20 with hypertension
items.text: **Lipids from 20 with hypertension** on iOS only (not in USPSTF 2022 / the web module): keep or remove.

items.title: iOS vaccination and questionnaire lines
items.text:
**iOS vaccination and questionnaire lines** (influenza, tetanus, pneumococcal, AUDIT-C, PHQ-9):
kept pending decision D6; the web does not show them.

items.title: NG12 on iOS
items.text:
**NG12 on iOS**: the same decisions as the web (fix-web-screening.md items 2, 3, 8, 9): direct
2WW for rectal bleeding ≥ 50, ferritin cut-off 45 µg/L, age ≥ 50 as the post-menopausal stand-in,
oral-iron wording, and the card showing the 1.1.0 criteria only.

items.title: NG12 card placement and inputs
items.text:
**NG12 card placement and inputs**: Diagnosis tab; reads HPI, examination and assessment text
and the associated-symptom chips; dismissal lasts for the app session only.

items.title: Known-cancer suppression
items.text:
**Known-cancer suppression** also reads the working diagnosis on iOS (the web reads the
assessment and past history).

items.title: ABCD² removed from the TIA recommendations
items.text: **ABCD² removed from the TIA recommendations** (NICE NG128); NIHSS / mRS still recommended for TIA.

items.title: Litres in the paediatric dose rule
items.text:
**Litres in the paediatric dose rule** — not changed here (item 4 dropped); noted for the agent
porting `planSafety`: `suppressAdultDoses` does not treat "1 L" fluid volumes as doses, and it
skips whole lines that mention urine output (so "Hartmann's 1 L stat then titrate to urine
output" keeps the adult volume for a child).

items.title: Default reference ranges
items.text:
**Default reference ranges** (adults 18+, marked "default — replace with your laboratory's
ranges"; to be replaced by Laboratory Services Ltd's own ranges before go-live):

| Analyte | Unit | Range | Critical |
|---|---|---|---|
| WBC | ×10⁹/L | 4.0–11.0 | — |
| Haemoglobin | g/dL | male 13.0–17.0, female 12.0–15.5 | < 8.0 (any sex) |
| Platelets | ×10⁹/L | 150–400 | < 50 |
| INR | — | 0.8–1.2 | > 2.5 |
| D-dimer | µg/L FEU | ≤ 500 | — |
| CRP | mg/L | ≤ 5 | — |
| Sodium | mmol/L | 135–145 | < 120 or > 155 |
| Potassium | mmol/L | 3.5–5.3 | < 2.5 or > 6.0 |
| Urea | mmol/L | 2.5–7.8 | — |
| Creatinine | µmol/L | male 59–104, female 45–84 | > 300 (any sex) |
| eGFR | mL/min/1.73m² | ≥ 60 | — |
| Calcium (total) | mmol/L | 2.20–2.60 | < 1.75 or > 3.0 |
| Magnesium | mmol/L | 0.70–1.00 | — |
| Glucose | mmol/L | 3.9–7.8 (random) | < 3.0 or > 20.0 |
| HbA1c | % | ≤ 5.6 | — |
| Bilirubin | µmol/L | ≤ 21 | — |
| ALT / AST | U/L | ≤ 40 | — |
| ALP | U/L | 30–130 | — |
| GGT | U/L | ≤ 65 | — |
| Albumin | g/L | 35–50 | — |
| Amylase | U/L | ≤ 100 | — |
| Lipase | U/L | ≤ 60 | — |
| LDH | U/L | ≤ 200 | — |
| Lactate | mmol/L | ≤ 2.0 | > 3.9 (i.e. ≥ 4.0 at one decimal) |
| Troponin I / T / unspecified | ng/L | ≤ 14 | > 52 |
| CEA | ng/mL | ≤ 5 | — |
| CA 19-9 | U/mL | ≤ 37 | — |
| AFP | ng/mL | ≤ 10 | — |
| CA-125 | U/mL | ≤ 35 | — |
| PSA (male) | ng/mL | ≤ 4 | — |

Points to decide: the troponin I ULN of 14 ng/L is below most high-sensitivity troponin I
assays' 99th percentile (it over-flags; the laboratory's assay value should replace it); the
LDH ULN of 200 U/L matches the Light's-criteria number the app used, but LDH ranges depend on
the method; glucose 3.9–7.8 assumes a random sample; ESR, ferritin and the other analytes have
no default (the laboratory's own flag applies).

items.title: Critical limits
items.text:
**Critical limits.** They reproduce iOS `LabPanel.hasCriticalValues`, so the web and iOS agree.
Should the practice add others (for example WBC < 1.0 or > 30, bilirubin, amylase / lipase, a
paediatric set)? None were added without your decision.

items.title: Escalation expectation for a critical result
Matching rule
items.text:
**Matching rule**: automatic filing only on exact MRN + date of birth; a person matches
everything else; a mismatch can be filed only with an explicit identity confirmation. Also:
whether the laboratory will send the practice MRN (AM-######) in PID-3 / Patient.identifier with
type MR — without it every result goes to reconciliation.

items.title: LOINC map
items.text:
**LOINC map** (`loinc.ts`, 100+ codes) and the label fallback: to be checked against the codes
the laboratory actually sends.

items.title: Flags never downgrade the laboratory
items.text:
**Flags never downgrade the laboratory** (practice range or the laboratory's flag, whichever is
more abnormal), and the report-import / decision-layer / TG18 / tumour-marker / Light's
consumers reading the practice ranges once entered.

items.title: Retention
items.text:
**Retention** of dismissed reconciliation rows (identity of people who may not be patients of
the practice) and of the message log (no bodies). Proposed: kept indefinitely like the record,
for audit, pending your decision.

items.title: Grade labels
items.text:
**Grade labels.** Works: tai chi, yoga, MBCT. Modest: slow breathing, acupuncture,
time-restricted eating. No benefit shown: cupping, detox teas / colon cleanses. **IV vitamin
drips are labelled "Mixed"** (briefing §6); the brief for this change asked for them under "No
benefit shown", but the verdict table (§8) does not list them and §6 grades them Mixed. Choose one.

items.title: Trigger conditions
The ≥ 65 threshold
items.text: **The ≥ 65 threshold** for "older adult" (tai chi).

items.title: The < 6 h sleep threshold
items.text: **The < 6 h sleep threshold** (strictly less than 6; 6 h does not trigger).

items.title: BMI ≥ 30
items.text:
**BMI ≥ 30** for time-restricted eating, and the decision to **show it with the fasting safety
note** (rather than hide it) when diabetes is treated with insulin or a sulfonylurea.

items.title: Fasting-prompt wording and scope
The three draft articles
items.text:
**The three draft articles**, for approval or edits: fasting with diabetes; exercise and
mind-body practices; detox teas, cleanses and vitamin drips. The fasting article lists signs of
low blood sugar and urgent-care signs (low blood sugar that does not settle, fainting, severe
dehydration) that are general knowledge, not taken from the briefing.

items.title: Questionnaire
items.text:
**Questionnaire**: the wording of the two questions, the timing follow-up, the option labels
("Vitamin drips", "Breathing exercises"), and the templates that ask them.

items.title: Citation details written from memory
items.text:
**Citation details written from memory** (not in the briefing's §10):
- **"IDF-DAR 2021"** — the briefing names "international diabetes guidance (IDF-DAR)" in §4
  with no year and no numbered reference. The year 2021 and the title "Diabetes and Ramadan:
  Practical Guidelines" are from memory. Used in the two diabetes prompts, the time-restricted
  eating note, and as the source of the fasting article.
- The volume/page details for Saper 2017 (167:85-94), Kuyken 2016 (73:565-74) and Liu 2022
  (386:1495-1504) are from §10 as written. Huang 2023 and Vickers 2012 have no volume/page in
  §10 and none was added. "24 RCTs, RR 0.76" and "HR 0.69" are from §4.
- The slow-breathing, cupping / detox / IV-drip and night-shift / sleep items cite the briefing
  itself, because §10 lists no primary reference for them.
- The detox article's only source is the practice briefing (2026).

items.title: Governance defaults
Minimum counts and shrinkage strength
items.text:
**Minimum counts and shrinkage strength:** priors ≥ 10 cases, Dirichlet concentration 200,
change of tier; likelihoods ≥ 20 cases, 20 pseudo-cases, change ≥ 0.10.

items.title: Reminder
items.text: **Reminder:** 14 days after completion, only after an operation or pathology.

items.title: Triggers
items.text:
**Triggers:** what counts as "operation" (web: CPT code / procedure name / peri-operative
procedure / Assessment procedures; iOS: procedural visit types or an operation date within 30
days) and "pathology" (biopsy, histology, histopathology, cytology, FNA, core needle, frozen
section).

items.title: Triage mapping to one scale
items.text:
**Triage mapping to one scale** (web urgent/priority/review; iOS emergency/urgent/priority →
emergency/urgent/soon), and using the clinician's retrospective urgency as the reference
standard.

items.title: Match rule
items.text:
**Match rule:** PANE id when both sides have one, else the ICD-10 3-character category. For
example K80 (gallstones) does not match K81 (cholecystitis).

items.title: Decision-band grading
items.text:
**Decision-band grading:** treat + done and observe / not-for-patient + not done agree; test
bands are not graded.

items.title: iOS push
items.text:
**iOS push:** confirm iOS stays local for now, or ask for the push loop as a follow-up (needs
device testing).

items.title: Governance only (behaviour-neutral move, identical outputs before and after). Confirm — clinical rules in
items.text:
Governance only (behaviour-neutral move, identical outputs before and after). Confirm — clinical rules in
`clinical-content/rules/*.json` are now the single source for both platforms, and edits there go
through the same registry versioning and sign-off as before.

items.title: Who may sign
items.text:
**Who may sign.** Doctor and admin accounts may record decisions (the database refuses
everyone else); nurses may read them. An admin account is not necessarily a clinician: should
admins be able to approve clinical content, or doctors only? (Relates to D6: who signs off
clinical content.)

items.title: What counts as reviewed
items.text:
**What counts as reviewed.** A rule set is written into the registry only when every item
linked to it is approved or approved with an amendment; pending, rejected, **deferred** and
changed items all hold it back. Confirm that a deferral should block, and that an amended
approval counts as approved (the amendment is recorded in section I and still needs a content
change to implement it).

items.title: Links between items and rule sets
items.text:
**Links between items and rule sets** as listed above, including the whole of SURGEON-DECISIONS
A counting towards `ios-diagnosis-radiation-engine` (its registry entry cites "SURGEON-DECISIONS
A"), so that rule set needs 87 approvals.

items.title: Review interval
items.text:
**Review interval.** `nextReviewDue` is set to 12 months after the last decision (the
registry's default), for every rule set.

items.title: Attestation wording
items.text: **Attestation wording:** "I have reviewed this item against the cited source."

items.title: Grades
items.text:
**Grades** of the 41 supplement rules (conservative: major for bleeding / serotonin / transplant
levels; moderate for kava, valerian, ashwagandha, echinacea, ginseng hypoglycaemia; contraindicated for
ephedra + MAOI). Candidates to discuss: kava + benzodiazepine (coma case reports) as major; echinacea +
immunosuppressant as major in transplant recipients; St John's wort + calcineurin inhibitor as
contraindicated.

items.title: Prompt thresholds
items.text:
**Prompt thresholds:** ALT / AST ≥ 120 U/L (3 × ULN 40); Hb < 12 / < 13 g/dL (WHO); K < 3.5, Na < 135;
blood lead ≥ 5 µg/dL; and the fever-only trigger for the IV-drip prompt (may be noisy).

items.title: Caribbean bush teas — add with sources?
items.text:
**Caribbean bush teas — add with sources?** Candidate plants, NOT active rules: cerasee (Momordica
charantia), soursop leaf (Annona muricata), noni (Morinda citrifolia), aloe, moringa, sorrel / hibiscus,
fever grass (lemongrass). Today they fall under "Bush tea / herbal remedy (unspecified)".

items.title: Patient text
items.text:
**Patient text:** exact wording for emergency / urgent surgery; whether the pre-op assessment visit
and minor procedures under local anaesthetic should carry the herbal paragraph (both deliberately left
without it; the assessment visit's "no sedation wording" rule would need changing).

items.title: Vitamin E and fish oil
items.text: **Vitamin E and fish oil** (not in the briefing): add as catalogue items / bleeding rules?

items.title: Brand and synonym names
items.text:
**Brand and synonym names** added only where certain (Kyolic, Kwai, EGb 761, Tebonin, Tanakan,
Ginsana, Echinaforce, KSM-66; drug brands per SmPC): confirm local availability.

items.title: Pharmacist review of the new drug classes (hazard H-08), as for the existing interaction list
items.text: Pharmacist review of the new drug classes (hazard H-08), as for the existing interaction list.

items.title: TG18 auto-fill
items.text:
**TG18 auto-fill** reads the record and pre-ticks criteria (Grade III whenever one organ rule is
met). Web additions to the iOS organ rule: metaraminol and vasopressin count as vasopressors.
Age ≥ 75 (TG18 wording; iOS uses > 75). Duration > 72 h read from "N days / hours" in the HPI.

items.title: Colonic stent contraindications
items.text:
**Colonic stent contraindications**: perforation / free gas, peritonitis *or peritonism
(guarding / rebound)*, ischaemia / pneumatosis, closed loop, caecum ≥ 12 cm; right-sided =
caecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure (transverse colon is not classed).

items.title: Asymptomatic screening request
items.text:
**Asymptomatic screening request** rule (triage): an explicit "no symptoms" statement plus a
screening / family-history topic and no symptom chip; the features that keep the flag.

items.title: Family-history entries
items.text: **Family-history entries** no longer count as a higher-risk comorbidity in triage.

items.title: SIGN 104 high-risk list
items.text:
**SIGN 104 high-risk list** used for lap chole prophylaxis (acute cholecystitis, clinical
jaundice, pregnancy, pancreatitis, immunosuppression); "per local antimicrobial policy" instead
of a named drug.

items.title: Mesh hernia prophylaxis
items.text: **Mesh hernia prophylaxis** not routine in average-risk elective repair (HerniaSurge 2018).

items.title: Complicated appendicitis
items.text:
**Complicated appendicitis**: pip-tazo 3–5 days after source control (maximum 7), metronidazole
removed from the post-operative line.

items.title: NSAID exclusions
items.text:
**NSAID exclusions** in templates: renal impairment (CKD, dialysis, eGFR < 60), age ≥ 75, heart
failure, peptic ulcer / GI bleed history, anticoagulant.

items.title: Renal VTE line
items.text:
**Renal VTE line**: enoxaparin 20 mg once daily if CrCl < 30; UFH or renally adjusted LMWH on
dialysis per renal team.

items.title: GI bleed instability
items.text:
**GI bleed instability** definition: SBP < 90, shock index > 1, Hb < 80 g/L, or collapse /
syncope / large volume / clots in the history; stable bleeding → Oakland / Glasgow-Blatchford
first.

items.title: Pre-op clotting
items.text:
**Pre-op clotting** (NICE NG45): only liver disease, vitamin K antagonist or heparin, bleeding
disorder, clinical jaundice (sign, symptom or bilirubin ≥ 34 µmol/L) or emergency surgery; no
routine test with a DOAC.

items.title: Triage over-triage
items.text:
**Triage over-triage** (not changed): whether keyword red flags with normal observations (NEWS2
low band) should mean same-day / 24–48 h review rather than "emergency now", once the emergency
layer recognises strangulated hernia, variceal bleeding and acute severe colitis directly.

items.title: Appendicectomy induction prophylaxis
items.text:
**Appendicectomy induction prophylaxis** (not changed): pip-tazo + metronidazole doubles
anaerobic cover — choose a single regimen.

items.title: Penicillin allergy
items.text:
**Penicillin allergy**: penicillin lines in prompts are withheld (replaced), not annotated; the
cephalosporin / carbapenem caution after anaphylaxis is stated.

items.title: Diabetic foot flags (rules 1.4.0)
items.text:
**Diabetic foot flags (rules 1.4.0)**: ulcer / wound as priority (1 working day), gangrene /
infection / osteomyelitis / exposed bone as urgent; "spreading redness" removed.

items.title: Hyperkalaemia bands
items.text: **Hyperkalaemia bands** (UKKA 2023): no shift therapy at 5.5–5.9; salbutamol only ≥ 6.5.

items.title: Two-level Wells
items.text: **Two-level Wells** wording and "D-dimer unhelpful after recent surgery and in pregnancy".

items.title: Cirrhosis with ascites
items.text:
**Cirrhosis with ascites** before hernia repair: planned inpatient repair after hepatology
optimisation (ascites control, TIPS considered).

items.title: Wording changes to the emergency layer
items.text:
**Wording changes to the emergency layer** (1.0.1): torsion exploration "if torsion cannot be
excluded"; anticoagulated head injury "drug-specific reversal if intracranial bleeding is
confirmed".

items.title: No stat test from a considered diagnosis
items.text:
**No stat test from a considered diagnosis.** Stat tests of an unconfirmed leading differential
are held back (not downgraded) until the diagnosis is confirmed; they remain in the reference
ManagementPanel. Alternative: show them as "urgent — confirm the diagnosis first".

items.title: Fallback to the leader
items.text:
**Fallback to the leader** when the confirmed diagnosis has no protocol (e.g. O26.83 renal colic
in pregnancy). The ManagementPanel deliberately shows nothing in that case; the suggestions
(badged "leading differential", no stat) do use the leader.

items.title: Leader threshold 20%
items.text: **Leader threshold 20%** for seeding (the ManagementPanel's threshold; previously any top-3).

items.title: SummaryTab now fills only from a confirmed diagnosis
items.text:
**SummaryTab now fills only from a confirmed diagnosis** (it used an unlocked working
diagnosis too).

items.title: Dictionary "Start"
items.text:
**Dictionary "Start"** still pre-adds stat/urgent tests to the ordered list (unchanged
behaviour from UX C3), now adapted and without caveated tests. Should it become suggestions?

items.title: New protocols
items.text:
**New protocols** — `aortoenteric_fistula` (ESVS 2020; kind emergency; no ICD mapping) and
`hsp_iga_vasculitis` (SHARE 2019; D69.0 for children and adults; steroids "may be considered"
for severe abdominal pain or orchitis; monitoring "at least 6 months, 12 if urinary
abnormalities persist"). Content and citations not verified by the surgeon.

items.title: Protocol additions
items.text:
**Protocol additions** — MRI pelvis for perianal Crohn's (ECCO-ESGAR 2019), CT for an
obstructed/strangulated femoral hernia (WSES 2017), blood cultures in amoebic liver abscess.

items.title: Age ≥ 65 acute-abdomen lactate line
items.text:
**Age ≥ 65 acute-abdomen lactate line** (ESVS 2017; NELA): trigger = K-code protocol with
immediate-phase steps, assessment not "elective".

items.title: Paediatric fluids
items.text:
**Paediatric fluids**: the ≥ 50 mL (or any litre volume) threshold that separates a fluid volume
from a drug dose in mL in a fluid line; the exact string is shared with iOS.

items.title: Pregnancy-test suppression
items.text: **Pregnancy-test suppression**: age < 10 or > 55, male, or a recorded pregnancy.

items.title: anaplastic_thyroid alias
items.text:
**`anaplastic_thyroid` alias** to the thyroid carcinoma protocol; **`sah` left unaliased** until
the syncope ranking is fixed.

items.title: Ranking rule
items.text:
**Ranking rule**: safety → decision → score; within safety the fixed order weight (under 16) →
allergy → pregnancy → renal function → anticoagulant last dose → supplements. In particular:
**weight before allergy status in a child**, and the supplements question and the anticoagulant's
last dose counted as safety-critical (they top 136 of 433 vignettes).

items.title: Decision-gap probe values
items.text:
**Decision-gap probe values** (the "worst plausible" value used to ask "would it change the
answer?"): CFS 7, ASA IV, eGFR 25, pregnant, BMI 42, HAS-BLED 3, NEWS2 7; a probe that changes no band
demotes the input to score completeness ("Refines …").

items.title: Discriminator placement
items.text:
**Discriminator placement**: in the decision tier only while no working diagnosis is confirmed; after
confirmation it ranks after score completeness.

items.title: NEWS2 rule
items.text:
**NEWS2 rule**: a partial set always lists the missing parameters; no observations at all are listed
only in an emergency, inpatient or post-operative setting. ACVPU and air / oxygen count as parameters
(not recorded = missing, as H-04 already decided).

items.title: Safety thresholds and scopes
items.text:
**Safety thresholds and scopes**: pregnancy 12–55 (female) with ionising imaging, a planned medicine
or a planned procedure; weight under 16 regardless of a planned drug; allergy status always; what counts
as a recorded pregnancy status (a pregnancy test result, "not pregnant", post-partum, hysterectomy,
post-menopausal).

items.title: Term lists
items.text:
**Term lists** in the rules JSON: renally cleared / NSAID drugs (including morphine, tramadol,
gabapentin, pregabalin, DOACs, LMWH, metformin, aminoglycosides, vancomycin, nitrofurantoin, lithium,
digoxin, aciclovir, trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole, methotrexate), anticoagulants, ionising imaging and
contrast terms, "last dose" wording, insulin names, the history and examination-finding terms used for
auto-fill (read negation-aware; ≤ 4-character terms as whole words).

items.title: Auto-fill thresholds
Findings filled from text
items.text:
**Findings filled from text** (affirmed only, never "false"): migration, anorexia, nausea / vomiting,
RIF pain / tenderness, rebound, melaena, syncope, haemoptysis, DVT signs, confusion; history: cancer,
DVT / PE, heart failure, IHD, cerebrovascular disease, insulin-treated diabetes, liver disease, IBD,
varicose veins, OCP / HRT, immobility.

items.title: Actions
items.text:
**Actions**: "Add test" names — "Urine pregnancy test (β-hCG)", "U&E with creatinine and eGFR",
"Full blood count (FBC)", "C-reactive protein (CRP)", "Liver function tests (LFTs)",
"Prothrombin time (PT/INR)", "Ultrasound abdomen (RUQ)", "Ferritin" — added as suggested (web: the
suggested-order path; iOS: an investigation with status "Suggested", noted "(what's missing)").

items.title: Wording
items.text: **Wording** of every what / why line (`text` and `groups` in the rules JSON).

items.text: **Replacement**: the iOS NG12 card no longer shows the ferritin check (the row carries it).
